about: What SecuRAX itself demonstrates for each control in the BFSI control library. proven = a file plus a test/CI check shows it; partial = SecuRAX supplies part, the rest is the organisation's; any control not listed is the organisation's (people, process, contracts, sites).

AM-007.note: pinned images, hashed vendored skills; a full SBOM is not yet produced

AS-001.note: SAST, secrets scan, IaC and container scans, admission gate on every change

AS-002.note: authenticated, rate-limited, guarded AI API with idempotency and backpressure

AS-005.note: automated diff and mutation checks; human review is the organisation's

AS-006.note: supply-chain gate for third-party skills, OpenSSF Scorecard and SLSA

AS-008.note: dependency and container vulnerability scanning in CI

AS-012.note: strict security headers on the site and the app

AUD-004.note: continuous control monitoring on every build and in the cockpit

BCP-003.note: verified backups; immutable/air-gapped copies are the organisation's

BCP-010.note: restore verifies checksums; the safe-update journey proves rollback with data intact

CR-002.note: post-quantum readiness map and crypto-agility plan

CR-006.note: hybrid post-quantum key exchange on the HTTPS edge

CR-007.note: hybrid PQ key exchange in transit; long-term stored data is the organisation's to classify

DP-002.note: PII (PAN, Aadhaar, cards, phones) redacted from AI traffic; enterprise DLP is wider

DP-003.note: regulated data is routed only to in-country models

DP-005.note: cross-border routing blocked or re-routed by data class; cloud region allow-list

DP-007.note: TLS on every web connection and internal hop

DP-010.note: personal data masked before any model sees it

DP-015.note: verified, optionally encrypted backups; not immutable storage

ET-001.note: model registry, NIST AI 600-1 map, evaluations before release

ET-008.note: advanced supply-chain controls (pinning, hashing, Scorecard, SLSA)

ET-010.note: every GenAI call is guarded: injection rails, PII redaction, residency, tool-call guard

GOV-006.note: the regulatory incident clock supports the crisis plan; the plan itself is the organisation's

GOV-010.note: the cockpit is a board-ready dashboard of measured posture

GOV-014.note: requirement-by-requirement maps with evidence, checked in CI

IAM-002.note: the gateway can require an MFA claim on every token

IAM-012.note: every authenticated call is audited with its subject

IAM-013.note: placeholder keys and sync tokens are replaced with random ones on start

IAM-014.note: OIDC/JWT and API keys, roles, lock-out at the AI gateway

IR-001.note: 6-hour CERT-In clock with drafts and sealed evidence

IR-003.note: every applicable regulator's deadline, as data

IR-005.note: incident drafts per regulator; scenario playbooks are the organisation's

IR-007.note: game days that break components on purpose

IR-008.note: blameless postmortems with owned, dated actions

NS-001.note: separate edge and model networks; no published model ports

NS-005.note: remote access over Tailscale (zero-trust mesh), never a public port

RM-001.note: the cockpit backlog ranks open gaps; the enterprise register is the organisation's

SOC-003.note: MISP organ and the KEV snapshot; sector feeds are the organisation's

SOC-005.note: AI-SOC triage mapped to MITRE ATLAS / ATT&CK

SOC-008.note: automated triage and playbooks for AI events

TP-002.note: the incident clock carries the escalation deadlines

VM-003.note: continuous scanning of code and images in CI

VM-004.note: red-team scorecard and purple-team loop for the AI channel

ET-101.note: ./securax ai stop|resume: one model or all AI, no restart, reason shown and logged; cockpit lamp while stopped

ET-102.note: inventory with tier, owner, third party, explainability, validation due, change-since-validation, 10-year decommission records, and models served at the gateway but not listed (para 21); board approval is the organisation's

ET-103.note: every answer carries X-AI-Generated; a stopped model tells callers a human handles it. The hand-off itself is the organisation's

ET-104.note: third_party flagged per model and validated by our own red-team; contracts and audit rights are the organisation's

ET-105.note: a model changed after validation is flagged; every change goes through PR, CI and the impact map; the impact assessment document is the organisation's

ET-106.note: failover ladder across providers ending in the private local model; the kill switch message names the fallback

RM-101.note: KRIs with thresholds and RAG bands, trends, dark-cockpit lamps

ET-107.note: residency routing, PII masking, audit and per-caller allowance at the gateway; the payments data itself is the organisation's
